---
title: "CanadaLogin Signal Check"
subtitle: "For the two-week period of October 5 to 18"
author: "EDCP Data and Research Team"  # colin.douglas@cds-snc.ca
date: "2026-10-19"
params:
  edition: 9
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
    theme: [cosmo, _fonts.scss]   # _fonts.scss: self-hosted brand fonts
    toc: false
    fig-width: 8
    fig-height: 3.4
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
---

```{r setup}
# Queries are frozen to the October 5 - 18, 2026 period.
source("../R/connection.R")
source("../R/branding.R")
source("../R/colours.R")
source("../R/publishing.R")
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(dbplyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(scales)
})

con <- connect_athena()

# Watermark date: the date this report is first created.
report_date <- as.Date("2026-10-19")

period_start <- as.Date("2026-10-05")
period_end <- as.Date("2026-10-18")

# Google Analytics is exported on a two-day lag, so its view ends a day early.
ga_period_end <- as.Date("2026-10-17")

# Monday of the launch week; the service went live Apr 22.
series_start <- as.Date("2026-04-20")

# The hourly IBM Verify event stream went live (data pipeline PR #94).
stream_live <- as.Date("2026-10-05")

# A signature error (CSIAQ0197E) blocked most ATIP sign-ins; cause still
# under investigation with ATIP and IBM.
jwt_start <- as.Date("2026-09-30")
jwt_end <- as.Date("2026-10-02")

# The Monday the weekly SSO series starts, two weeks before the incident week.
sso_series_start <- as.Date("2026-09-07")

# Readership tracking began on this day.
tracking_start <- as.Date("2026-07-23")

prev_end <- period_start - 1

# Public relying parties from the rp schema. Several application names map to
# one service, so aggregate after joining this.
relying_parties <- load_relying_parties(con) |>
  filter(!is_internal)
public_parties <- distinct(relying_parties, application_name, service_name)

# Figure 1 --------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Users by first day, from the event stream. This role cannot filter partitions,
# so the day comes from the time string. "UNKNOWN" has no account behind it.
stream_daily <- tbl(
  con, in_schema("ibm_verify_events_raw", "authentication_activity")
) |>
  filter(!is.na(subject), subject != "", subject != "UNKNOWN") |>
  group_by(subject) |>
  summarise(first_day = min(substr(time, 1L, 10L)), .groups = "drop") |>
  count(first_day, name = "new_users") |>
  collect() |>
  transmute(day = as.Date(first_day), new_users = as.double(new_users)) |>
  arrange(day) |>
  mutate(users = cumsum(new_users)) |>
  filter(day <= period_end)

# Weekly points at each week's Sunday; the count only rises within a week.
weekly_users <- stream_daily |>
  mutate(week_end = monday_of(day) + 6) |>
  group_by(week_end) |>
  summarise(users = max(users), .groups = "drop")

stream_total <- weekly_users$users[weekly_users$week_end == period_end]
new_this_period <- stream_total -
  weekly_users$users[weekly_users$week_end == prev_end]

# Launches behind the two big steps in the user count. Both ATIP services
# launched together, so they share one marker.
launches <- relying_parties |>
  mutate(label = case_when(
    service_name == "GC Digital Talent" ~ "GC Digital Talent\nlaunch",
    startsWith(service_name, "ATIP") ~ "ATIP services\nlaunch"
  )) |>
  filter(!is.na(label)) |>
  group_by(label) |>
  summarise(day = min(launch_date), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(nrow(launches) == 2L)

# The first day the stream count reached 60,000.
milestone <- 60000
milestone_day <- min(stream_daily$day[stream_daily$users >= milestone])

# Figure 2 --------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Successful SSO events to each public service, by week. total_logins also
# counts failed attempts, which ballooned during the incident.
atip_name <- "ATIP Online Request Service"

service_colours <- c(
  "GC Digital Talent" = unname(colors$brand["blue"]),
  "ATIP Online Request Service" = unname(colors$brand["orange"]),
  "ATIP Online Management Tools" = unname(colors$brand["yellow"]),
  "IRIS" = unname(colors$brand["forest"]),
  "MyCGC" = unname(colors$brand["green"]),
  "CED Client Space" = unname(colors$brand["sky"]),
  "VAC Healthshare" = unname(colors$brand["grey"]),
  "Other services" = unname(colors$greyscale[3])
)

# From launch, so ATIP's best week is checked against its whole history.
sso_daily <- tbl(con, in_schema("ibm_verify", "app_login_counts")) |>
  filter(from_date >= series_start, from_date <= period_end) |>
  transmute(
    day = as.Date(from_date),
    application_name,
    sso_events = as.double(successful_logins)
  ) |>
  collect() |>
  inner_join(public_parties, by = "application_name")

# rp.alias is overwritten every weekday, and a dropped row would quietly
# remove a service rather than raise anything.
stopifnot(all(
  setdiff(names(service_colours), "Other services") %in%
    sso_daily$service_name
))

weekly_sso_all <- sso_daily |>
  mutate(
    week_end = monday_of(day) + 6,
    service_group = if_else(
      service_name %in% names(service_colours), service_name,
      "Other services"
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(week_end, service_group) |>
  summarise(sso_events = sum(sso_events, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

weekly_sso <- filter(weekly_sso_all, week_end > sso_series_start)

weekly_totals <- weekly_sso |>
  group_by(week_end) |>
  summarise(sso_events = sum(sso_events), .groups = "drop")

atip_weekly <- weekly_sso_all |>
  filter(service_group == atip_name) |>
  arrange(week_end)

incident_week <- monday_of(jwt_start) + 6
atip_incident_week <- atip_weekly$sso_events[
  atip_weekly$week_end == incident_week
]
atip_peak_week <- slice_max(atip_weekly, sso_events, n = 1)
stopifnot(atip_peak_week$week_end >= period_start)

# ATIP this period against the two weeks before the incident week.
atip_in <- function(from, to) {
  sum(sso_daily$sso_events[
    sso_daily$service_name == atip_name &
      sso_daily$day >= from & sso_daily$day <= to
  ])
}
atip_this <- atip_in(period_start, period_end)
atip_before <- atip_in(sso_series_start, sso_series_start + 13)
atip_change <- atip_this / atip_before - 1

# The token error as users saw it, from Google Analytics. Weekly events, since
# daily distinct users cannot be summed across days.
jwt_code <- "CSIAQ0197E"
jwt_message <- "Signature verification of the JSON Web Token (JWT) failed."
jwt_daily <- tbl(con, in_schema("google_analytics", "error_events")) |>
  filter(
    error_code == !!jwt_code,
    as.Date(date) >= sso_series_start, as.Date(date) <= ga_period_end
  ) |>
  group_by(date) |>
  summarise(
    events = sum(eventcount, na.rm = TRUE),
    # A floor: totalusers cannot be summed across rows.
    users = max(totalusers, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  collect() |>
  mutate(
    day = as.Date(date), events = as.double(events), users = as.double(users)
  )

weekly_jwt <- jwt_daily |>
  mutate(week_end = monday_of(day) + 6) |>
  group_by(week_end) |>
  summarise(events = sum(events), .groups = "drop") |>
  right_join(distinct(weekly_sso, week_end), by = "week_end") |>
  mutate(events = coalesce(events, 0))

# A shorter repeat the next week.
jwt_repeat <- jwt_daily |>
  filter(day > jwt_end + 1, users >= 50) |>
  arrange(day)
stopifnot(nrow(jwt_repeat) >= 1L)

# Figure 3 --------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Dwell per edition over its first 14 days. Group on pagepath_redacted, never
# pagepath, which holds the private token.
dwell_marks <- c(1, 5, 15, 30, 60, 120, 300, 600)
edition_window_days <- 14

edition_events <- tbl(
  con, in_schema("google_analytics", "meta_page_events")
) |>
  filter(
    page_kind == "signal_check",
    eventname %in% !!c("page_view", paste0("read_", dwell_marks, "s")),
    as.Date(date) >= tracking_start,
    as.Date(date) <= ga_period_end
  ) |>
  group_by(date, pagepath_redacted, pagetitle, eventname) |>
  summarise(events = sum(eventcount, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  collect() |>
  mutate(
    day = as.Date(date),
    events = as.double(events),
    published = as.Date(
      sub(".*/([0-9]{8})_signal-check\\.html$", "\\1", pagepath_redacted),
      "%Y%m%d"
    )
  ) |>
  # Editions sent before tracking began are missing their first days. Views
  # before the send day are the team reviewing the draft.
  filter(
    published >= tracking_start,
    day >= published, day < published + edition_window_days
  )

# Edition number from the page title's "#N", as the Readership dashboard does.
edition_numbers <- edition_events |>
  distinct(published, pagetitle) |>
  mutate(edition = as.integer(sub(".*#([0-9]+).*", "\\1", pagetitle))) |>
  filter(!is.na(edition)) |>
  distinct(published, edition)

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(edition_numbers$published))

edition_totals <- edition_events |>
  inner_join(edition_numbers, by = "published") |>
  group_by(edition, eventname) |>
  summarise(events = sum(events), .groups = "drop")

# Share of page views still open at each milestone, per edition and pooled.
dwell_curve <- function(totals) {
  views <- sum(totals$events[totals$eventname == "page_view"])
  reached <- vapply(
    dwell_marks,
    \(s) sum(totals$events[totals$eventname == paste0("read_", s, "s")]),
    numeric(1)
  )
  tibble(
    seconds = dwell_marks, reached = reached, page_views = views,
    share = reached / views
  )
}

edition_curves <- edition_totals |>
  group_by(edition) |>
  group_modify(\(d, ...) dwell_curve(d)) |>
  ungroup()

edition_labels <- edition_numbers |>
  arrange(edition) |>
  mutate(panel = paste0(
    "Signal Check #", edition, ", ", format(published, "%b "),
    as.integer(format(published, "%d"))
  ))
edition_curves <- edition_curves |>
  inner_join(edition_labels, by = "edition") |>
  mutate(panel = factor(panel, edition_labels$panel))

# When half the page views were still open, log-interpolated between the
# milestones either side of 50%, matching the Readership dashboard.
median_read <- function(seconds, share) {
  above <- which(share >= 0.5)
  if (length(above) == 0L) return(0)
  i <- max(above)
  if (i == length(seconds)) return(Inf)
  step <- (share[i] - 0.5) / (share[i] - share[i + 1L])
  exp(log(seconds[i]) + step * (log(seconds[i + 1L]) - log(seconds[i])))
}

# "20 seconds" under a minute, otherwise minutes to one decimal.
format_read <- function(seconds, short = FALSE) {
  if_else(
    seconds < 60,
    paste0(round(seconds), if (short) " s" else " seconds"),
    paste0(round(seconds / 60, 1), if (short) " min" else " minutes")
  )
}

edition_medians <- edition_curves |>
  group_by(edition, panel) |>
  summarise(
    page_views = first(page_views),
    median_seconds = median_read(seconds, share),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# The most-read edition, which held its readers the least.
most_read <- slice_max(edition_medians, page_views, n = 1)
stopifnot(most_read$median_seconds == min(edition_medians$median_seconds))

# As a compound adjective: "a 57-second read", "a 1.1-minute read".
read_length <- function(seconds) {
  if_else(
    seconds < 60, paste0(round(seconds), "-second"),
    paste0(round(seconds / 60, 1), "-minute")
  )
}

# The previous edition's median, for the closing line's joke.
previous_median <- edition_medians$median_seconds[
  edition_medians$edition == params$edition - 1
]

pooled_curve <- dwell_curve(edition_totals)
pooled_views <- pooled_curve$page_views[1]
pooled_median <- median_read(pooled_curve$seconds, pooled_curve$share)
share_at <- function(s) pooled_curve$share[pooled_curve$seconds == s]

# Sessions by where they came from, every edition since tracking began.
edition_sources <- tbl(
  con, in_schema("google_analytics", "meta_page_traffic")
) |>
  filter(
    page_kind == "signal_check",
    as.Date(date) >= tracking_start,
    as.Date(date) <= ga_period_end
  ) |>
  group_by(sessionsource) |>
  summarise(sessions = sum(sessions, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  collect() |>
  mutate(sessions = as.double(sessions)) |>
  arrange(desc(sessions))

stopifnot(
  edition_sources$sessionsource[1] == "slack",
  all(c("teams", "email") %in% edition_sources$sessionsource)
)
slack_share <- edition_sources$sessions[1] / sum(edition_sources$sessions)
```

This is the **CanadaLogin Signal Check**, our read on CanadaLogin every two
weeks. This edition covers three things. First, how many users CanadaLogin
has, counted with our new IBM Verify event stream. Second, how the ATIP
Online Request Service recovered from a short outage. Third, in the spirit of
the season, how you read this report.

**CanadaLogin passed `r comma(milestone)` users, and we can trust the count
again.** In past editions, we asked you to read our user counts with caution.
That changed on `r format_long_date(stream_live)`, when our new IBM Verify
event stream went live. Every hour, it brings in IBM Verify's record of each
sign-in, user by user, so we count users directly instead of relying on a
running total from IBM. Each user appears in these data only as a scrambled
code. We never see names, email addresses, phone numbers or IP addresses,
yet we can still count each user once. By `r format_long_date(period_end)`, CanadaLogin had
**`r comma(stream_total)`** users since launch, and
**`r comma(new_this_period)`** of them joined in these two weeks. The count
passed `r comma(milestone)` on `r format_long_date(milestone_day)`.

```{r users-since-launch}
#| fig-alt: |
#|   Line chart of CanadaLogin users since the April 2026 launch, one point per
#|   week, from the IBM Verify event stream. Dashed lines mark the launch of
#|   GC Digital Talent in June and the ATIP services in September, each
#|   followed by a jump, and the stream going live on October 5. The line ends
#|   at 61,845 users on October 18.
stream_latest <- slice_max(weekly_users, week_end, n = 1)

users_plot <- ggplot(weekly_users, aes(week_end, users)) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = c(stream_live, launches$day), linetype = "dashed",
    colour = "grey40"
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = launches, aes(x = day - 2, y = stream_total * 0.6, label = label),
    hjust = 1, size = 3, colour = "grey30", lineheight = 0.9
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text", x = stream_live - 2, y = stream_total * 0.3, hjust = 1,
    size = 3, colour = "grey30", label = "Event stream\nlive"
  ) +
  geom_line(colour = colors$brand["blue"], linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = stream_latest, colour = colors$brand["red"], size = 3) +
  geom_text(
    data = stream_latest, aes(label = comma(users)),
    colour = colors$brand["red"], hjust = 1.15, vjust = -0.8,
    fontface = "bold", size = 3.6
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = comma, limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))
  ) +
  scale_x_date(
    breaks = seq(series_start + 6, period_end, by = "week"),
    date_labels = "%b %d", expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.03))
  ) +
  theme_cds() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "Users since launch",
    title = paste("CanadaLogin passed", comma(milestone), "users"),
    subtitle = "Users since launch, by week, from the IBM Verify event stream."
  )

add_cds_logo(add_watermark(users_plot, date = report_date,
                           edition = params$edition))
```

**ATIP use set a new high after a short sign-in issue.** From
`r format_long_date(jwt_start)` to `r format_long_date(jwt_end)`, most
sign-ins to both ATIP services failed a digital signature check that
confirms each request really came from the service (red). A shorter repeat followed on
`r format_long_date(min(jwt_repeat$day))` and
`r as.integer(format(max(jwt_repeat$day), "%d"))`. No other service was
affected, both recovered quickly, and ATIP and IBM are still looking into
the cause (see the
[incident channel](https://gcdigital.slack.com/archives/C0C7W2PF4UT)). In
the week ending `r format_long_date(atip_peak_week$week_end)`, the Online
Request Service, where Canadians ask for government records, had
**`r comma(atip_peak_week$sso_events)`** successful SSO events, its busiest
week yet, and over these two weeks its use was
**`r percent(atip_change, accuracy = 1)`** higher than in the two weeks
before the issue.

```{r sso-by-service}
#| fig-height: 5.4
#| fig-alt: |
#|   Two stacked charts on a weekly axis, September 13 to October 18, 2026:
#|   successful SSO events to public services, with the two ATIP services in
#|   orange and yellow, above red bars of signature errors (CSIAQ0197E). In the
#|   week ending October 4, errors jump to about 10,000 and both ATIP services
#|   drop, with a smaller rise of about 900 the next week. The ATIP Online
#|   Request Service then reaches its highest week by October 18.
week_limits <- c(min(weekly_sso$week_end), max(weekly_sso$week_end)) +
  c(-3.5, 3.5)
week_axis <- scale_x_date(
  breaks = unique(weekly_sso$week_end), date_labels = "%b %d",
  limits = week_limits, expand = expansion(0)
)
incident_band <- annotate(
  "rect", xmin = incident_week - 3.5, xmax = incident_week + 3.5,
  ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = colors$greyscale[3], alpha = 0.2
)

sso_plot <- ggplot(
  # The first level stacks on top, so the grey band caps each bar.
  mutate(weekly_sso, service_group = factor(
    service_group, rev(names(service_colours))
  )),
  aes(week_end, sso_events, fill = service_group)
) +
  incident_band +
  geom_col(width = 5) +
  geom_text(
    data = weekly_totals, aes(label = comma(sso_events), fill = NULL),
    vjust = -0.5, size = 3.2
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text", x = incident_week, y = Inf, vjust = 1.4, size = 3,
    colour = "grey30", label = "ATIP issue"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = service_colours, breaks = names(service_colours), name = NULL
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = comma, limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))
  ) +
  week_axis +
  theme_cds() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "Successful\nSSO events",
    title = "ATIP use dipped during its sign-in issue, then hit a new high",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Successful SSO events to public services (top) and signature ",
      "errors (bottom), by week."
    )
  )

jwt_plot <- ggplot(weekly_jwt, aes(week_end, events)) +
  incident_band +
  geom_col(width = 5, fill = colors$brand["red"]) +
  geom_text(aes(label = comma(events)), vjust = -0.5, size = 3.2) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = comma, limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.3))
  ) +
  week_axis +
  theme_cds() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()) +
  labs(
    x = "Week ending", y = "Signature\nerrors",
    subtitle = paste0(jwt_code, ': "', jwt_message, '"')
  )

# Stacked on one shared axis; the legend sits beside both.
combined <- patchwork::wrap_plots(
  sso_plot, jwt_plot, ncol = 1, heights = c(2.4, 1), guides = "collect"
)

# Taller figure, so the logo height fraction is scaled to match the others.
add_cds_logo(
  add_watermark(combined, date = report_date, edition = params$edition),
  height = 0.13 * 3.4 / 5.4
)
```

**Readers keep a Signal Check open for about a minute.** It is almost
Halloween, the spooky season, and what is more spooky than self-reflection?
So we turned our data on ourselves, using Google Analytics events to analyze
the `r comma(pooled_views)` Signal Check views over the last three months.
The median view lasted **`r format_read(pooled_median)`**, and
**`r percent(share_at(600), accuracy = 1)`** stayed open for 10 minutes or
more. Our closing line usually promises a two-minute read, and
`r percent(share_at(120), accuracy = 1)` of views last the full two minutes.
The link we post in Slack brings in more readers than either the Teams link
or what we send out via email, at `r percent(slack_share, accuracy = 1)` of
visits.

```{r readership-dwell}
#| fig-height: 4.8
#| fig-alt: |
#|   Six small line charts, one per Signal Check from #3 to #8, each showing
#|   the share of its page views still open from 1 second to 10 minutes over
#|   its first two weeks, with the other editions' curves pale behind it and
#|   each panel's median time labelled. Medians run from about 1 to 2
#|   minutes, except Signal Check #6, the most read, at 20 seconds.
mark_labels <- c("1s", "5s", "15s", "30s", "1m", "2m", "5m", "10m")

# Every other edition's curve, drawn pale behind each panel's own.
other_curves <- edition_curves |>
  rename(other = panel) |>
  tidyr::crossing(panel = levels(edition_curves$panel)) |>
  filter(as.character(other) != panel) |>
  mutate(panel = factor(panel, levels(edition_curves$panel)))

panel_counts <- edition_medians |>
  transmute(
    panel,
    label = paste0(
      comma(page_views), " views\nmedian ",
      format_read(median_seconds, short = TRUE)
    )
  )

dwell_plot <- ggplot(edition_curves, aes(seconds, share)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey55",
             linewidth = 0.35) +
  geom_line(data = other_curves, aes(group = other),
            colour = colors$greyscale[4], linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_line(colour = colors$brand["blue"], linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(colour = colors$brand["blue"], size = 1.4) +
  geom_text(
    data = panel_counts, aes(x = 600, y = 1, label = label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = 3, lineheight = 0.9,
    colour = "grey35"
  ) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = dwell_marks, labels = mark_labels) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = percent, limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 3) +
  theme_cds() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Time the page was open and visible", y = "Page views still open",
    title = "The median Signal Check view lasts about a minute",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Each edition over its first two weeks (blue), with the others behind ",
      "it. Google Analytics."
    )
  )

# Taller figure, so the logo height fraction is scaled to match the others.
add_cds_logo(
  add_watermark(dwell_plot, date = report_date, edition = params$edition),
  height = 0.13 * 3.4 / 4.8
)
```
